title: Does one neuron mean one feature?
hook: Find distinct inputs with the same activation.

doesNotKnow: h=max(0,T+S−.5). T/S are binary features. Does h=.5 uniquely identify T?

objective: Compute this finite polysemantic-neurons model, compare earned countercases, and explain its stated boundary.

claims.text:
polysemantic-neurons

**Identity / target / source:** `ai:polysemantic-neurons` → `ai-polysemantic-neurons` → `src/demos/ai/ai-polysemantic-neurons`; source `company/domains/proposals/2026-10-18-ai-map-expansion.json#concepts/154`; brief `company/domains/briefs/2026-10-19-ai-next30e.md#25-polysemantic-neurons`. **Packet:** I2. **Level / prerequisites:** core; `ai:hidden-layers-xor`.

**Nearest / distinct payoff:** hidden-layers-xor combines features for classification; this demonstrates two unrelated declared features sharing an indistinguishable neuron activation.

**Computed primary model:** Two independent binary stimulus flags TriangleT and StripedS. Single supplied neuron h=ReLU(T+S−.5). Cases(1,0) and(0,1) both yield.5; neither flag gives0; both gives1.5. An observer of h=.5 alone cannot tell which of the two flags is present.

**Countercase / boundary:** Two separate supplied units hT=T,hS=S distinguish the singleton cases. This is a deliberately constructed coordinate/feature collision, not a trained neuron or evidence that any particular real neuron has these semantic roles. Activation magnitude alone need not uniquely identify an input property.

**Prediction / transfer recall:** Predict whether h=.5 proves Triangle; recall h1.5 identifies both flags only under this complete declared4-input model, not universally.

**Intervention / retained witness:** Toggle each original code-native shape/pattern flag computes weighted sum, ReLU and activation-only decoder ambiguity; Separate units shows the distinguishing pair while retaining the shared.5 witness. Label feature flags independently of the neuron coordinate.

**Source obligation:** [Elhage et al. original Toy Models PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2209.10652), opened2026-10-19, “Definitions and Motivation” and toy ReLU embedding/unembedding setup. Only the local constructed activations/directions below are admitted; the paper’s trained phase transitions, real-model prevalence and semantic feature identities are not reproduced.
